chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about the scattering (of sweets/nuts) from sugar and almonds and their like, is it permissible to eat it? He said: It is disliked to eat what is seized (or scattered as plunder).

key_terms.النِّثَارِ: Scattering or throwing things loosely, often referring to sweets or nuts thrown in celebration.
key_terms.انْتُهِبَ: Was seized or plundered; here used metaphorically for items scattered and grabbed casually.
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: It is disliked (makruh), a juristic ruling indicating something is discouraged but not forbidden.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat scattered sweets and nuts thrown during celebrations according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on consuming sweets and nuts scattered during celebrations, ruling that it is disliked (*makruh*) to eat what is 'seized' or 'plundered' (*al-muntahab*). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between casual consumption and the act of grabbing items in a manner resembling *ghulul* (plunder) or hasty, undignified seizing, thereby preserving the etiquette of sharing and preventing waste or conflict among participants.
